verdict.rationale: MotherDuck's billing docs say idle Ducklings shut down automatically (zero idle cost), and per-second billing with sub-100ms cold starts means idle compute should not burn money overnight. Fixed per-workload instance sizes also cap the resources any one workload can use, and SQL usage views plus a billing dashboard give visibility into consumption. However, nothing in the evidence shows a budget, spend cap, alerting resource monitor, or query timeout that would actively stop a runaway query; the monitoring tools only report usage after the fact. Missing for 10: budgets/spend caps, alerting resource monitors, runaway-query timeouts or kill controls, detailed auto-suspend configuration docs, independent corroboration.
